sb_prompt: WHAT DO YOU THINK ABOUT CURRENT OR RECENT AMERICAN ACTIONS IN LATIN AMERICA
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Hi, I'm calling about the Latin America topic. How are you?
ParticipantB: Hey, I'm good. How about you?
ParticipantA: Pretty good, yeah. Just got off a double shift at the restaurant. It was crazy tonight.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? That sounds intense. What kind of stuff do you do?
ParticipantA: I mostly just serve tables, keep it simple. But tonight we had this group of tourists from Brazil. They were laughing their heads off.
ParticipantB: Oh, nice! That's actually kind of interesting. I work as a plumber, so I see a lot of people from different places.
ParticipantA: Wait, a plumber? No way! That sounds totally different from serving tables. How did you end up doing that?
ParticipantB: Well, I made up my mind years ago without really knowing why. Just felt like it was the right thing to do.
ParticipantA: That's cool. So you've been doing it for a long time then?
ParticipantB: Yeah, since I was like twenty-three. It's steady work, you know?
ParticipantA: Yeah, steady is good. Sometimes I hate the job, but the money helps a lot.
ParticipantB: Exactly. And you know, being a plumber means I travel sometimes. I've fixed pipes in Mexico and down in Central America.
ParticipantA: Oh wow, really? Have you been to South America?
ParticipantB: No, not South America. Just the northern part of Central America, like Guatemala and Honduras.
ParticipantA: That's neat. I actually had a table from there last week. We talked about politics.
ParticipantB: Oh? What did they say?
ParticipantA: They said the US government is getting too involved. They feel like we're trying to control their elections or something.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that happens a lot. You know, here in the US, sometimes people think they have to dictate things everywhere.
ParticipantA: Right? And it's not always welcome. One guy said, "You guys can stop interfering, please."
ParticipantB: Yeah, I agree. It's like... we shouldn't be running their country for them. It's not our job.
ParticipantA: Totally. It makes me wonder if we should just stay out of it more.
ParticipantB: Exactly. Just let them handle their own problems.
ParticipantA: Yeah. Though sometimes it feels like we have to do something. Like when there's corruption.
ParticipantB: True. But maybe the solution isn't sending people over to fix it. Maybe just sending aid or helping them build up on their own.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. Aid without the politics.
ParticipantB: Yeah. And you know, the people I meet down there, they're just normal folks trying to live.
ParticipantA: For sure. My Brazilian table was just happy to have a nice meal and chat. They didn't want a lecture.
ParticipantB: Exactly. Just a nice meal and chat. That's all most people want.
ParticipantA: I agree. No politics needed. Just good food.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I've got to go, I've got a leaky pipe somewhere.
ParticipantA: Okay, same here. Thanks for talking about it.
ParticipantB: You too. Bye.
ParticipantA: Bye.
